method.description: Coming Soon is a film-level Seattle theatrical calendar over a 90-day Pacific-local window. Four independent evidence facts are tracked: AMC Coming Soon catalog membership (national), Seattle-area AMC theater bookings, TMDB US theatrical releases, and published Reel Seattle showtimes. classification remains pipeline/source state; relevance_tier and in_recommended drive the curated Recommended list (confirmed_local, locally_announced, strongly_expected). The public artifact also ships a broader All releases film-calendar slice (weak_national_only / below-popularity AMC∩TMDB) while TMDB-only, special-programming, and local repertory/series stay analysis-only. Confirmed local bookings are classified as release-like vs local programming; ambiguous niche Seattle openings are retained without a TMDB popularity gate. strongly_expected requires AMC catalog ∩ TMDB US theatrical plus TMDB popularity at/above the configured floor. Engagement SKUs (Q&A, Fan First, Early Access, Fan Event) consolidate under the parent film.

presentation.overview:
The morning after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination, Jane Elliott divided her all-white third-grade class in Riceville, Iowa, by eye color. Her lesson in discrimination made her a national figure and a target.

Nearly sixty years later, JANE ELLIOTT AGAINST THE WORLD finds her as funny and combative as ever. She stands with students, teachers, and families in Temecula, California, fighting restrictions on teaching race and history. At home, her daughters ask her to acknowledge what her refusal to stay silent has cost them.

The woman who spent a lifetime asking others to change must now try to change herself.

'The supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting.'  Sun Tzu

MAATRUBHUMI: MAY WAR REST IN PEACE is a story of extraordinary courage on the battlefield and the equally powerful battles fought by families back home.

At its heart is one man's unbreakable resolve -- his courage, sacrifice and determination to stand his ground against impossible odds, never giving an inch, while striving for peace against the threat of war.
To the officers who serve under him, he is more than a commander. He is a father figure, a leader they trust with their lives, and a man they would follow into the depths of hell.

A story of valour, brotherhood, sacrifice and the human spirit  where the greatest victories are not always won by fighting.

Winner of the U.S. Documentary Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival and hailed by Werner Herzog as 'truly groundbreaking', NUISANCE BEAR places viewers inside the world of a polar bear to deliver a cinematic pressure cooker and an urgent parable for our times. 

Filmmakers Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman follow a polar bear in Churchill, Manitoba -- the self-styled 'Polar Bear Capital of the World' -- forced to navigate tourists, wildlife officers and hunters as climate change pushes it into town.
  
Guided by Inuit narrator Mike Tunalaaq Gibbons, whose perspective resists simplification, Nuisance Bear overturns the conventions of the nature documentary to ask: when a sacred predator is branded a 'nuisance,' who truly belongs in this shared landscape?

presentation.overview: THE DEPARTED is set in South Boston, where the state police force is waging war on organized crime.  Young undercover cop Billy Costigan (Leonardo DiCaprio) is assigned to infiltrate the mob syndicate run by gangland chief Costello (Jack Nicholson).   While Billy is quickly gaining Costello's confidence, Colin Sullivan (Matt Damon), a hardened young criminal who has infiltrated the police department as an informer for the syndicate, is rising to a position of power in the Special Investigation Unit.  Each man becomes deeply consumed by his double life, gathering information about the plans and counter-plans of the operations he has penetrated.  But when it becomes clear to both the gangsters and the police that there's a mole in their midst, Billy and Colin are suddenly in danger of being caught and exposed to the enemy - and each must race to uncover the identity of the other man in time to save himself.

Set against the nostalgic backdrop of an early 2000s Telugu village, Rayavalasa is an emotionally engaging rural drama that brings together love, friendship, family relationships, village rivalries, and unexpected twists.The story revolves around Raju, a kind-hearted young man who lives with his grandmother, cherishing his friendships and leading a simple life while carrying the emotional burden of his parents' tragic past. His peaceful world takes an unexpected turn when Rani, the village president's daughter, returns from the city with a dream of establishing a school for the village children. As their destinies become intertwined, long-standing political rivalries, jealousy, ego, and hidden agendas begin to disrupt the harmony of the village. A carefully planned conspiracy puts Raju and Rani's reputations at stake, triggering a chain of unexpected events that changes their lives forever. Caught between love, friendship, betrayal, and powerful village politics, Raju must confront injustice and fight to protect his dignity, relationships, and everything he holds dear.
Blending rooted Telugu nativity, nostalgic village celebrations, vibrant folk music, heartfelt emotions, and gripping dramatic twists, Rayavalasa promises an engaging theatrical experience that celebrates the innocence of village life while exploring the complexities of human relationships.

presentation.overview:
We only imagine and invent ourselves. 

Oscar nominee Sandra Huller (Anatomy of a Fall, The Zone of Interest) takes on her most powerful role yet in ROSE, writer-director Markus Schleinzer's transcendent new film. 

In 17th century Germany, a mysterious soldier arrives in an isolated village, laying claim to an abandoned farmstead with the intent to settle down. Unbeknownst to the residents, this outsider is Rose, born a woman yet living as a man. Upon moving in and resolutely taming the land, he realizes the sole way to secure his position is to marry into the community. Yet taking a wife (Caro Braun) gives rise to suspicions even as they grow close, propelling events towards a reckoning.

Meticulously rendered in stunning black-and-white, ROSE transports us to a world unlike any other to convey the universal value of personal freedom. In her Silver Bear-winning star turn, Sandra Huller embodies a self-defining protagonist whose profound fluidity and humanity resonates through the past and into the present. Matching this emphatic performance with exquisite technique, Austria's Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards is a boundary-breaking fable from a true craftsman.

website and impulsively switch homes for the holiday. Iris moves into Amanda's L.A. house in sunny California as Amanda arrives in 
the snow covered English countryside. Shortly after arriving at their destinations, both women find the last thing either wants or expects: a new romance. Amanda is 
charmed by Iris' handsome brother Graham (Law) and Iris, with inspiration provided by legendary screenwriter Arthur (Wallach), mends her heart when she meets film 
composer Miles (Black).

In 1974, the New York City music scene was shocked into consciousness by the violently new and raw sound of a band of misfits from Queens called The Ramones. Playing in a seedy Bowery bar to a small group of fellow struggling musicians, the band struck a chord of disharmony that rocked the foundation of the mid-seventies music scene. This quartet of unlikely rock stars traveled across the country and around the world connecting with the disenfranchised everywhere, while sparking a movement that would resonate with two generations of outcasts across the globe. Although the band never reached the top of the Billboard charts, they managed to endure by maintaining a rigorous touring schedule for twenty-two years. 4K Re-release.

presentation.overview: Set at the height of World War I in the shadows of the Belgian trenches, Lukas Dhont's COWARD unfolds as an epic, intimate journey of youthful self discovery through love, art, and survival. Pierre arrives at the front lines as a young soldier eager to find his footing in a world consumed by violence. Everything changes when he meets Francis, a kindred spirit whose vision of staging a front-line theater show unlocks a world Pierre never knew existed. What begins as a fleeting escape from the harsh reality of the trenches soon blossoms into a tender, emotional love story, anchored by the undeniable chemistry of breakout actors Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne. As the world burns around them, their stage becomes a sanctuary of innocence and devotion. COWARD beautifully explores the fine line between fear and fortitude for soldiers in search of a promised glory, ultimately asking: when the world demands brutality, is walking away for love the truest act of bravery?

Confident grade-schooler Fujino draws comics for her school newspaper, earning the admiration of her classmates. When her artwork is surpassed by her reclusive peer Kyomoto, she becomes obsessed with honing her skills, eventually burning out and giving up drawing altogether. But when Fujino finally meets Kyomoto, she discovers that Kyomoto has been her devoted fan all along. Bound by their shared passion, they spend irreplaceable years drawing manga together until a fateful event changes their lives forever.

From Palme d'Or winner Hirokazu Koreeda, Look Back is a love letter to the artistic process, hand-written in ink on paper, and a meditation on how mutual pursuit of a craft creates the deepest etches in our memory.

presentation.overview: Immerse yourself in the heart of a fascinating country where ancient traditions and modernity coexist in perfect harmony. From bustling metropolises like Tokyo to serene places like Kyoto, this journey unveils the many facets of the Japanese archipelago. Through encounters and discoveries, the film leads us to iconic sites steeped in history and emotion, such as Hiroshima and the sacred island of Miyajima, as well as to more peaceful regions, including the majestic landscapes of the Japanese Alps. Between ancient temples, ultramodern cities, and breathtaking panoramas bathed in the colors of autumn, our adventurers Serge and Johanne offer a sensitive and authentic perspective on Japan.

The sun is down.  The boat is dead.  There's no cell service.  And there's someone standing, staring, from both shores.  Written and directed by Joshua Giuliano, RIVER stars Jane Levy (Evil Dead), Jessica Rothe (Happy Death Day) and Max Mattern (Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy) as three estranged siblings who reunite in their hometown after the death of their father. As they set out to scatter his ashes at his favorite spot on a remote river, the trip devolves into a waking nightmare. Dane DiLiegro (Prey) also stars in the film.

Currently with a 94% critics rating on Rotten Tomatoes, RIVER was acquired by Universal Pictures and Blumhouse Atomic Monster following an electrifying launch at Midnight Madness at the Toronto International Film Festival. This release establishes a meaningful, new collaboration between Universal Pictures, Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Independent Film Company and Shudder, bringing them together for the expanded theatrical release of Joshua Giuliano's debut feature. 

Universal Pictures, Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Independent Film Company present RIVER, a Shudder Original Production, in association with Upgrade. RIVER is produced by Spooky Pictures' Steven Schneider and Eat the Cat's Nick Antosca and Alex Hedlund. The film is executive produced by Allegheny Image Factory's Jeffrey Tinnell and Robert Tinnell, Upgrade's Matt Brodlie and Jonathan Kier, Ben Ross and Blumhouse Atomic Monster's Jason Blum.

The film, about a country western star in free fall, is set to star Glen Powell and Cristin Milioti. Judd Apatow will direct. Apatow and Powell wrote the script together.

Apatow will produce through his longstanding Apatow Productions overall deal with the Studio. Apatow's relationship with the Studio dates back to his 2005 directorial debut, The 40-Year-Old Virgin, and he has since directed Knocked Up, Funny People, This is 40, Trainwreck and The King of Staten Island for the Studio.

Powell and Dan Cohen will produce through Barnstorm's first look deal with the Studio. Powell's relationship with the Studio originates with his starring role in Twisters, which overperformed against all industry expectations, becoming the biggest opening for a natural disaster film ever at the domestic box office and grossing $267.8 million overall in the domestic box office.

Kevin Misher will produce through Misher Films. Misher has a storied history with Universal Pictures, where he was President of Production from 1996-2001 and supervised production for some of the Studio's most acclaimed features, including Erin Brockovich, The Fast and the Furious, Meet the Parents, and The Mummy. Misher subsequently formed Misher Films, where he has been producing a variety of films over the past two decades, including Fighting With My Family, Coming 2 America and You People.
